components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The one action a screen wants. The gradient slides and the button lifts 2px on hover.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary{display:inline-flex;align-items:center;justify-content:center;gap:8px;min-height:50px;padding:13px 28px;border:1px solid transparent;border-radius:999px;font-family:Manrope,'Segoe UI',Arial,sans-serif;font-size:13px;font-weight:800;letter-spacing:.09em;text-transform:uppercase;color:#fff;cursor:pointer;background:linear-gradient(115deg,#e4142f 0%,#c8102e 38%,#6b0016 78%,#05070a 100%);background-size:200% 200%;background-position:0% 50%;box-shadow:0 8px 18px rgba(200,16,46,.22),0 18px 40px rgba(200,16,46,.16);transition:transform .25s cubic-bezier(.22,1,.36,1),box-shadow .25s cubic-bezier(.22,1,.36,1),background .25s cubic-bezier(.22,1,.36,1)}.ds-btn-primary:hover{background-position:100% 50%;transform:translateY(-2px);box-shadow:0 12px 24px rgba(200,16,46,.28),0 24px 50px rgba(200,16,46,.2)}.ds-btn-primary:focus-visible{outline:3px solid #c8102e;outline-offset:3px}.ds-btn-primary:active{transform:translateY(0)}

narrative.overview:
This is an institution that keeps receipts. A decree year, an associate-membership date, seven named directors, seven partners sorted by tier - the Lebanese Ice Hockey Federation's claim is that it is recognised, and the design's whole job is to let that claim land without raising its voice. The system reads like an official register that happens to be printed in the colours of a jersey: facts set in heavy uppercase display type, given room, and left alone.

The atmosphere is assured, documentary and unfussy, and it is warm rather than corporate. Nothing here performs enthusiasm. The off-white panels, the soft warm neutrals and the civic tone place this as a community body with international standing - not a startup, not a brand campaign. Where other sporting sites reach for montage and urgency, this one reaches for whitespace and a date. The primary visitor is deciding whether to attach their organisation's name to the federation; credibility does that work, not atmosphere.

Red is the exception that proves it. The palette is overwhelmingly ink on warm paper, and the jersey red appears only where the visitor is meant to act or orient. That restraint is the system's single most load-bearing decision: a red button means something here because almost nothing else is red.
keyCharacteristics: Heavy uppercase Archivo display type with negative leading (0.94) and tight tracking, set against a warm off-white
A near-monochrome page with cedar red held to roughly a tenth of any screen
Layered two-part shadows rather than one soft blur - depth that reads as printed, not floated
An 8pt spacing scale and a 1360px shell, with a fluid gutter from 20px to 84px
Self-hosted type and zero third-party requests, which is a published privacy commitment, not a performance tactic
Motion exists only as a response to the visitor

rules.name: The Ten Percent Rule
rules.body: Cedar Red covers roughly a tenth of any screen and never more. It belongs to eyebrows, primary actions, the active nav state, field focus, and one gradient word per hero. A red-backed section, a red card, or a red heading breaks it - and every one of those weakens the primary button, which is the only thing on the page the federation actually needs clicked.

rules.name: The Warm Neutral Rule
rules.body: Every grey in this system is warm. A cool grey background (#f5f5f5, #fafafa, anything with a blue cast) next to Bone reads as a mistake, not a variant. Chrome is the single cool exception and only ever appears on dark.

rules.name: The One Gradient Word Rule
rules.body: Exactly one word in an h1 may take the red gradient (h1 .accent, a 100 degree ramp from #ff5a70 through Cedar Red to Cedar Red Deep, via background-clip: text). One word, h1 only, once per page. It is a signature, and a signature used twice is a pattern. Gradient text anywhere else - h2, metrics, body, buttons - is forbidden.

rules.name: The Uppercase Ceiling Rule
rules.body: Uppercase stops at Title. Display, Headline, Label and Action are uppercase; Title and Body never are. Uppercase running text is unreadable and is the fastest way to make a credibility-first page look like a promotion.

rules.name: The Alternating Panel Rule
rules.body: Sections separate by background, not by border. White, then Bone, then white. A horizontal rule between two sections is redundant and is not used.

rules.name: The Two-Shadow Rule
rules.body: Every shadow has a contact layer and an ambient layer. A single-value box-shadow is not part of this system.

rules.name: The Pill-and-Panel Rule
rules.body: If the visitor clicks it, it is a pill. If the visitor reads it, it is a 16px panel. A rounded-rectangle button or a pill-shaped content card both break the vocabulary.

rules.name: The Response-Only Motion Rule
rules.body: Motion in this system answers the visitor - hover, focus, press, reveal on scroll. Nothing animates on its own. The one pre-existing exception is the 8px pulsing dot on the hero registration badge (pulse-dot, 2.4s, infinite); it is inherited, it is not a pattern, and no second ambient animation should join it.

rules.name: The Shared Variable Rule
rules.body: When two properties must stay aligned across breakpoints - a link's padding and its underline inset, a tile's width and its scroll step - they read from one custom property. Duplicating the number is how they drift.

dos: Do keep Cedar Red to roughly 10% of a screen: eyebrows, primary action, active nav, field focus, one hero word.
Do pair every shadow - a contact layer and an ambient layer, per the Two-Shadow Rule.
Do use pills for actions and 16px panels for content.
Do separate sections by alternating white and Bone backgrounds rather than by rules or dividers.
Do set every spacing value from the 8pt scale (--s-1 through --s-9), and every radius from the four named steps.
Do keep uppercase to Display, Headline, Label and Action; Title and Body stay sentence case.

Do self-host every font and asset. Zero third-party requests is a published commitment, and adding an external origin means updating cookies.html and introducing a consent requirement - it is a decision to raise, never a quiet addition.
Do run npm run contrast after any colour change; it reads the live tokens out of assets/styles.css, so it cannot drift from this file.
Do give collapsed tables a data-label on every cell so they become cards below 760px.
donts: Don't put gradient text anywhere but a single word in an h1. Not on h2, not on metrics, not on buttons.
Don't introduce a cool grey. Every neutral in this system is warm; Chrome is the only cool value and only on dark surfaces.
Don't add a second ambient animation. Motion responds to the visitor; the inherited pulsing badge dot is an exception, not a precedent.
Don't substitute the identity assets - the inline #cedar-mark SVG, the LIHF logo (assets/LIHF-01_edited.png), the flag strip, or the Archivo + Manrope pairing. These are fixed.
Don't fabricate proof. No testimonials, attendance figures, sponsorship prices, media lists or registration numbers exist in this project; a design pass does not get to invent them to fill a layout.
Don't let a red surface compete with the primary button.
Don't hardcode a hex that already exists as a token.
